subject: interpolate INLA posterior distribution across time

messages.author: bb0d51bd5af5ac0d
messages.subject: interpolate INLA posterior distribution across time
parts:
Hi there,

I'm doing a multivariate model with INLA for days with all variable observed, and now trying to interpolate across days for missing data (each day has a set of INLA predictions). Some days have 1 missing variable and some days has 2 missing variables, while the observed variables I used univariate INLA model to do prediction. 

My question here is where to get the prediction posterior distribution(which I think it's Gaussian) so that I could just interpolate the Gaussian distribution mean, sd for those missing variables.
Or, if there's better/easier way to do the interpolation?

toy example code for multivariate model:
    form <- y ~ 0 + intercept1 + intercept2 + intercept3 +
      f(s1, model = spde) + f(s2, model = spde) +  f(s3, model = spde) +
      f(s12, copy = "s1", fixed = FALSE, hyper = hyper) +
      f(s13, copy = "s1", fixed = FALSE, hyper = hyper) +
      f(s23, copy = "s2", fixed = FALSE, hyper = hyper)

Thanks,
Wenlong
